sentences.en: Over the past several years, I've explored hundreds of ideas on Hidden Brain
sentences.zh: 在过去的几年里，我在《隐藏的大脑》中探讨了数百个想法，

sentences.en: on how we can live better lives and have healthier relationships.
sentences.zh: 关于我们如何过上更好的生活以及建立更健康的伴侣关系。

sentences.en: Many of these ideas have felt provocative and insightful to me.
sentences.zh: 其中许多想法让我感到极具启发性和深刻性。

sentences.en: And as I interview guests and edit stories, I tell myself,
sentences.zh: 当我采访嘉宾和编辑故事时，我告诉自己，

sentences.en: I'm going to remember to apply these ideas to my own life.
sentences.zh: 我一定要记住将这些想法应用到我自己的生活中。

sentences.en: I'll follow the advice of researchers who've discovered how we can have better relationships.
sentences.zh: 我会遵循研究人员的建议，他们发现了我们如何才能拥有更好的关系。

sentences.en: I'll become a better colleague, parent, and citizen.
sentences.zh: 我会成为一个更好的同事、父母和公民。

sentences.en: But in my daily life, I forget to apply these lessons all the time.
sentences.zh: 但在我的日常生活中，我却总是忘记应用这些经验。

sentences.en: I'm impatient when I should be patient.
sentences.zh: 我该有耐心时却很不耐烦。

sentences.en: I'm distracted when I should be focused.
sentences.zh: 我该专心时却注意力不集中。

sentences.en: And I'm harsh with myself when I should be kind.
sentences.zh: 我该对自己好一点时却对自己很苛刻。

sentences.en: Psychologists sometimes call this the insight-action gap.
sentences.zh: 心理学家有时称之为“知行鸿沟”。

sentences.en: Knowing the right thing to do doesn't automatically mean we do the right thing.
sentences.zh: 知道正确的事情该怎么做，并不自动意味着我们就会去做正确的事情。

sentences.en: It isn't about hypocrisy per se.
sentences.zh: 这本身并不是关于虚伪。

sentences.en: It's that learning something and doing something involve different sets of brain muscles, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 而是说，学到一样东西和去做一样东西，可以说是动用了不同的一套大脑肌肉。

sentences.en: This is a very ancient idea and something that many religious and spiritual traditions have explored over the centuries.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常古老的观点，也是许多宗教和精神传统几个世纪以来一直在探讨的问题。

sentences.en: It's an old idea in art and literature, too.
sentences.zh: 这也是艺术和文学中一个古老的主题。

sentences.en: In the 16th century, William Shakespeare wrote,
sentences.zh: 在16世纪，威廉·莎士比亚写道：

sentences.en: I can easier teach 20 what were good to be done than be one of the 20 to follow my own teaching.
sentences.zh: “要教导二十个人什么是该做的事容易，要做那遵循自己教导的二十人之一却难。”

sentences.en: Today on the show, we explore the insight-action gap when it comes to our debates with our political opponents.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目中，我们来探讨在与政治对手辩论时存在的“知行鸿沟”。

sentences.en: It's the third episode in our series, Us 2.0, where we explore how we can become more effective talking across our differences.
sentences.zh: 这是我们“我们2.0”系列的第三集，在这一系列中，我们探讨了如何才能在存在分歧的情况下更有效地进行对话。

sentences.en: If you've missed any of the other episodes in this series, please be sure to check them out in this podcast feed.
sentences.zh: 如果你错过了本系列的任何其他单集，请务必在本播客动态中收听。

sentences.en: As we look at the news, it's hard not to feel like the world is constantly in flames.
sentences.zh: 当我们审视新闻时，很难不觉得世界正处于水深火热之中。

sentences.en: New conflicts pile on top of old conflicts, and antagonisms and disagreements seem to erupt everywhere.
sentences.zh: 新的冲突叠加在旧冲突之上，敌意和分歧似乎在各地爆发。

sentences.en: Conflicts also abound in our personal and professional lives.
sentences.zh: 在我们的个人生活和职业生活中，冲突也屡见不鲜。

sentences.en: How can we learn to diffuse them?
sentences.zh: 我们如何才能学会化解它们？

sentences.en: At Columbia University, psychologist Peter Coleman studies how minor disagreements turn into endless conflicts
sentences.zh: 在哥伦比亚大学，心理学家彼得·科尔曼研究了微小的分歧是如何演变成无休止的冲突的，

sentences.en: and how our own thought patterns can deepen divides or help us to mend fences.
sentences.zh: 以及我们自己的思维模式如何加深分歧或帮助我们消除隔阂。

sentences.en: Peter Coleman, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 彼得·科尔曼，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来参加。

sentences.en: Peter, in 2019, you were invited to attend a conference in Germany.
sentences.zh: 彼得，2019年，你应邀去德国参加了一个会议。

sentences.en: It looked at the emerging challenges in the Middle East and ideas to bring about peace.
sentences.zh: 会议探讨了中东地区新兴的挑战以及实现和平的想法。

sentences.en: Now, I understand the whole conference itself was focused on the idea of bringing together these very seasoned negotiators and diplomats.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，整个会议的核心就是把这些经验丰富的谈判代表和外交官汇聚到一起。

sentences.en: And the idea was that by putting all these experienced heads together,
sentences.zh: 其理念是，通过让所有这些富有经验的大咖齐聚一堂，

sentences.en: you would come up with initiatives that could be applied in the real world.
sentences.zh: 你们就能提出可以应用到现实世界中的倡议。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was a very impressive group of contributors.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一群非常令人印象深刻的参会者。

sentences.en: It was chaired by a senior person in the field who'd spent most of his life studying international conflict,
sentences.zh: 会议由该领域的一位资深人士主持，他毕生大部分时间都在研究国际冲突、

sentences.en: And he had assembled quite an impressive group of mostly, you know, former envoys or former ambassadors
sentences.zh: 他召集了一个相当强大的团队，其中大多是前特使或前大使，

sentences.en: and then academics like myself or people from think tanks.
sentences.zh: 还有像我这样的学者或智库人员。

sentences.en: And the idea was, yes, to offer current insights into what to do about the Middle East conflict.
sentences.zh: 我们的想法确实是为如何处理中东冲突提供当下的见解。

sentences.en: In particular, it was really about what can we do to make a difference in this sort of new era of more complex conflicts.
sentences.zh: 特别是，我们到底能做些什么，在这个更复杂冲突的新时代里发挥作用。

sentences.en: So the conference took a turn in one of the final sessions.
sentences.zh: 所以在其中最后一场会议上，情况发生了转变。

sentences.en: Paint me a picture of what happened.
sentences.zh: 给我描述一下当时发生了什么。

sentences.en: So this was a presentation by one of the co-chairs.
sentences.zh: 这是由其中一位联合主席作的报告。

sentences.en: He was an Israeli and he presented a paper, a kind of conceptual model of, you know, complex systems and conflict.
sentences.zh: 他是一位以色列人，他提交了一篇论文，一种关于复杂系统和冲突的概念模型。

sentences.en: And his respondent happened to be a former ambassador, a former Dutch ambassador, who also was a contributor to this.
sentences.zh: 而他的回应者恰好是一位前大使、一位前荷兰大使，他也是与会者之一。

sentences.en: And he said something like, given the fact that you're an Israeli and the book is focused on Israel and Palestine,
sentences.zh: 他说的大意是，鉴于你是一个以色列人，而且这本书的重点是以色列和巴勒斯坦，

sentences.en: my guess is we'll get more scrutiny than usual.
sentences.zh: 我猜我们会受到比平时更多的审查。

sentences.en: And that's about as far as he got in his comments.
sentences.zh: 他的发言也就进行到这里。

sentences.en: And at that point, my Israeli colleague stopped and said something like, what are you saying?
sentences.zh: 就在那时，我的以色列同事停了下来，说了一些类似“你这话是什么意思？”的话。

sentences.en: And the Dutch ambassador, you know, paused for a second and looked at me and said, well, what I was trying to say is, you know,
sentences.zh: 荷兰大使停顿了一秒钟，看着我说道，嗯，我本想表达的是，你知道的，

sentences.en: given that this is about Israel and you're an Israeli.
sentences.zh: 鉴于这是关于以色列的，而你又是一个以色列人。

sentences.en: And the Israeli colleague then came back and said, yes, but what exactly are you saying?
sentences.zh: 然后以色列同事反驳说，是的，但你具体是什么意思？

sentences.en: And he clearly was upset and triggered.
sentences.zh: 他显然很不高兴，被触怒了。

sentences.en: And it got tense from there.
sentences.zh: 从那以后气氛就变得紧张起来。

sentences.en: And, of course, we're a room full of peacemakers, peacebuilders or scientists that study that.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们满屋子都是调解员、和平建设者或研究这些的科学家。

sentences.en: And at some point, the other chair, the senior member of the group, tried to put a stop to it and said something like, all right, enough of this foolishness.
sentences.zh: 在某个时候，另一位主席、该团伙中的资深成员试图制止这种争吵，说了一句类似的话：好了，这种蠢事够了。

sentences.en: And he, the Israeli, said, I refuse to stop until I receive an apology.
sentences.zh: 而那位以色列人说，我拒绝停止，直到我得到道歉。

sentences.en: And the Dutch ambassador said, what are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 荷兰大使说，你在说什么？

sentences.en: I didn't do anything that requires an apology.
sentences.zh: 我没做什么需要道歉的事。

sentences.en: And so they went back and forth sort of like that for a little bit until the Israeli demanded an apology and said if he didn't get it, he would leave.
sentences.zh: 于是他们就这样来来回回争论了一会儿，直到以色列人要求道歉，并称如果得不到道歉他就会离开。

sentences.en: And at that point, he started to kind of pack up his belongings and put his things in his briefcase and backpack and was preparing to leave.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，他开始收拾自己的随身物品，把东西放进公文包和双肩包里，准备离开。

sentences.en: And if I understand correctly, what the Israeli negotiator was sort of upset about was the implication that because he was Israeli, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果我没理解错的话，这位以色列谈判代表感到不快的原因是暗示因为他是以色列人，

sentences.en: there would be special scrutiny that was attached to his work or to the work of the journal,
sentences.zh: 他的工作或该期刊的工作将会受到格外的审查，

sentences.en: that it would be seen with skepticism that he was biased in some way.
sentences.zh: 这会被人以怀疑的眼光看待，认为他在某种程度上带有偏见。

sentences.en: And he saw himself as being, you know, an objective scholar and whose work should be treated objectively.
sentences.zh: 而他认为自己是一名客观的学者，其工作应该受到客观对待。

sentences.en: And the fact that he was Israeli was beside the point.
sentences.zh: 他是否是以色列人根本无关紧要。

sentences.en: And the Dutch ambassador was saying, you know, let's pay attention to the reality on the ground.
sentences.zh: 而荷兰大使则在说，我们要关注地缘现实。

sentences.en: We're talking about the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
This is going to get more scrutiny.
sentences.zh: 这将会受到更多的审查。

sentences.en: And I can see from both people's points of view how they came to their positions.
sentences.zh: 我可以从两个人的角度理解他们为什么会持有各自的立场。

sentences.en: But I can also see how both people felt personally attacked in the situation.
sentences.zh: 但我也能理解双方在这场风波中都感到自己受到了人身攻击。

sentences.en: And then other people tried to sort of say, hey, you know, we're here to, you know, do good things for the world.
sentences.zh: 然后其他人试图打圆场说，嘿，你知道的，我们来这里是为了给世界做些好事。

sentences.en: And we're really here to try to understand and help the world, you know, with the peace process.
sentences.zh: 我们真的是为了试着理解世界，并通过和平进程帮助世界。

sentences.en: And let's try to put this conversation in that context.
sentences.zh: 让我们试着在这个背景下展开对话。

sentences.en: And so there were multiple attempts.
It was very interesting to kind of watch this because, again, it's a room full of very skilled people, but who were thrown into this by surprise and unprepared.
sentences.zh: 看着这一幕非常有趣，因为再次强调，这是一个坐满了能干之人的房间，但他们却在毫无准备的情况下出乎意料地陷入了这种境地。

sentences.en: And so at some point, the Israeli packed up and left.
sentences.zh: 所以在某个时刻，以色列人收拾东西离开了。

sentences.en: And the Dutch ambassador packed up and left.
sentences.zh: 荷兰大使也收拾东西离开了。

sentences.en: And the irony was that an hour or so before there was this paper on the role of identity and conflict.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，大约在一个小时前，这里刚宣读了一篇关于身份和冲突在其中所起作用的论文。

sentences.en: And here both of these individuals, I think, felt their identities, either their national identities and or their professional identities, attacked publicly.
sentences.zh: 而在这里，这两个人我认为都觉得他们的身份——无论是国家身份还是职业身份——受到了公开攻击。

sentences.en: And it really disabled them, their capacities to do what they would usually do, which is sort of manage the situation if other people were in that.
sentences.zh: 这确实让他们无所适从，丧失了他们通常会具备的能力，即如果其他人遇到这种情况，他们本可以去掌控局面的能力。

sentences.en: But they were facing it personally.
sentences.zh: 但他们自己正身陷其中。

sentences.en: Something similar happened to Peter in his own apartment building in Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 彼得在曼哈顿自己的公寓楼里也遭遇了类似的事情。

sentences.en: It involved a neighbor whom he calls David.
sentences.zh: 这涉及一位他称之为大卫的邻居。

sentences.en: I've known him probably for 10, 12 years, something like that.
sentences.zh: 我认识他大概有10、12年了，差不多这样。

sentences.en: So, you know, at times I'm on the elevator when he gets on.
sentences.zh: 所以，有时候当他上电梯时我正好在里面。

sentences.en: And what I noticed is that, you know, on occasion he started to make comments about, you know,
sentences.zh: 我注意到的是，你知道的，他偶尔会开始发表一些评论，

sentences.en: Me Too marches or Black Lives Matter marches or things that were happening in the streets of the city, kind of sarcastic remarks about those things or climate change.
sentences.zh: 关于“Me Too”游行、“黑人的命也是命”游行，或是城市街道上发生的事情，对这些事情发表讽刺性的言论，或者是针对气候变化。

sentences.en: And then at some point it became clear to me that he was a strong supporter of Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 然后有那么一段时间，我清楚地意识到他是唐纳德·特朗普的坚定支持者。

sentences.en: This had come just in a conversation in front of the building.
sentences.zh: 这是在楼前的一次交谈中得知的。

sentences.en: And then some of the things he started to say to me seemed rather extreme at some point.
sentences.zh: 接着，他开始对我说的一些话在某种程度上显得相当极端。

sentences.en: He mentioned something about having a lot of respect for Vladimir Putin, thinking he was, you know, a good leader.
sentences.zh: 他提到自己非常敬佩弗拉基米尔·普京，认为他是个好领导。

sentences.en: And, you know, so at some point I just started to think, okay, this, you know, I can't get into a back and forth conversation with him that's going to be constructive.
sentences.zh: 所以，有那么一段时间我只是觉得，好吧，我没法和他进行有建设性的来回对话了。

sentences.en: And so I basically just sort of pulled away, stopped engaging.
sentences.zh: 所以我基本上就是退缩了，不再与他交流。

sentences.en: If I'd see him, I'd smile, but I'd sort of just move on.
sentences.zh: 如果看到他，我会笑一笑，但就会直接走开。

sentences.en: I really just tried to unplug from the relationship.
sentences.zh: 我真的只是试着切断与这段关系的联系。

sentences.en: And was this because you were neighbors and you just didn't feel like this was the kind of conversation you wanted to have with the neighbor?
sentences.zh: 这是因为你们是邻居，而你觉得这根本不是你想跟邻居进行的对话吗？

sentences.en: Or was this also that your own politics and preferences were not aligned with his?
sentences.zh: 还是说这也因为你自己的政治立场和偏好与他并不一致？

sentences.en: I think it's a combination of both.
I think I didn't feel like he was someone that I could try to reason with because he would just sort of hold court, hold forth.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他不是那种我可以试着跟他讲道理的人，因为他总是喜欢高谈阔论、独占话语权。

sentences.en: And his opinions to me were just informed very differently from mine.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，他的观点形成的基础与我的大不相同。

sentences.en: And so I didn't see where we could go with this, which is why I felt like, yeah, I think I just need to disengage.
sentences.zh: 所以我看不到我们能在这上面谈出什么结果，这就是为什么我觉得，是的，我需要停止互动。

sentences.en: So there is some element of irony here, Peter, which is that you are someone who studies conflict and you are someone who studies disagreement.
sentences.zh: 所以这里面其实有一些讽刺意味，彼得，那就是你是一个研究冲突的人，也是一个研究分歧的人。

sentences.en: But your response to this person who disagreed with you was, I anticipate there's going to be conflict.
sentences.zh: 但你对这个与你意见相左的人的反应却是：我预料会发生冲突。

sentences.en: And my solution to this is to disengage with this person and try not to bump into him again.
sentences.zh: 而我的解决办法就是不理这个人，尽量避免再次撞见他。

sentences.en: And again, I think, you know, what most of us in this field of conflict resolution, peace building, you know, it's an eclectic field.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我认为我们这些从事冲突解决、和平建设领域的人——这是一个兼收并蓄的领域——

sentences.en: But most of us will say that when it happens to us, when we're in the middle of it and our passions get triggered or our politics get triggered, it's a different kind of problem.
sentences.zh: 但我们大多数人都会说，当这种事降临到我们自己头上，当我们身处其中，我们的情绪或政治立场被触动时，这就是一种不同性质的问题了。

sentences.en: It's somewhat what happened in Hamburg at this meeting of my colleagues on the Middle EaSt.
sentences.zh: 这有点像在汉堡的中东同事会议上发生的事情。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I think it's not something I'm proud of.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我认为这不是一件让我感到骄傲的事。

sentences.en: But I think my cost-benefit assessment at the time was, look, this isn't going anywhere.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我当时的成本效益评估是，听着，这谈不出什么结果。

sentences.en: I don't see him being open to listening or talking to me.
sentences.zh: 我看不出他有愿意倾听或与我交谈的意愿。

sentences.en: And I don't have the energy for this, so I'm out.
sentences.zh: 而且我也没有精力去应付这个，所以我退出了。

sentences.en: From international forums to neighbors in an apartment building, stray comments often lead to bigger probleMs.
sentences.zh: 从国际论坛到公寓楼里的邻居，三言两语往往会引发更大的问题。

sentences.en: Once conflicts erupt, it can be difficult to put the genie back into the bottle.
sentences.zh: 一旦冲突爆发，要想覆水难收就很难了。

sentences.en: When we come back, understanding the roots of the invisible forces that drive us apart.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我们将剖析将我们拉开的无形力量的根源。
您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: We all have moments in our lives when we have to take something we've learned and put it into practice in the real world.
sentences.zh: 我们的人生中都有这样的时刻：必须把学到的东西应用到现实世界中去。

sentences.en: Doing so, of course, is often a lot harder than we think it'll be.
sentences.zh: 当然，这样做往往比我们想象的要困难得多。

sentences.en: At Columbia University, social psychologist Peter Coleman got to witness the gap between theory and practice firsthand.
sentences.zh: 在哥伦比亚大学，社会心理学家彼得·科尔曼亲眼见证了理论与实践之间的鸿沟。

sentences.en: On October 7, 2023, the Palestinian militant group Hamas launched a surprise attack on southern Israel.
sentences.zh: 2023年10月7日，巴勒斯坦武装组织哈马斯对以色列南部发动了突袭。

sentences.en: It killed and wounded thousands of Israelis.
sentences.zh: 这造成了数千名以色列人伤亡。

sentences.en: The incident launched a bloody reprisal,
sentences.zh: 这一事件引发了血腥的报复，

sentences.en: with tens of thousands of Palestinians killed by Israeli bombs and a ground invasion of Gaza.
sentences.zh: 数万名巴勒斯坦人在以色列的轰炸和对加沙的地面进攻中丧生。

sentences.en: Peter, not long after the war in Gaza got underway, you were preparing to teach a class at Columbia University.
sentences.zh: 彼得，在加沙战争爆发后不久，你正准备在哥伦比亚大学上一门课。

sentences.en: Paint a picture for me of what happened that Wednesday evening.
sentences.zh: 给我描述一下那天周三晚上发生的事情。

sentences.en: So, conditions at Columbia escalated fairly rapidly after the October 7th incursion.
sentences.zh: 10月7日袭击事件发生后，哥伦比亚大学的情况迅速升级。

sentences.en: And we sort of felt it right away.
sentences.zh: 我们立刻就感受到了这一点。
抗议活动几乎接踵而至。

sentences.en: And several of my students come from different parts of the university.
sentences.zh: 我的几个学生来自大学的不同专业。

sentences.en: A big group of them were coming from the School of International Public Affairs.
sentences.zh: 他们当中有一大批人来自国际公共事务学院。

sentences.en: And they're often international students that are studying diplomacy and international affairs.
sentences.zh: 他们通常是正在学习外交和国际事务的国际学生。

sentences.en: And this group were coming into my class just before 5 p.m.
sentences.zh: 这群学生在下午5点之前来到我的课上，

sentences.en: in the evening and were looking shaken.
sentences.zh: 当时正值傍晚，他们看起来惊魂未定。

sentences.en: And they were looking at me with a concern.
sentences.zh: 他们带着担忧的眼神看着我。

sentences.en: And so, they came right up to me and started to describe their experience of the day,
sentences.zh: 于是，他们径直走到我面前，开始描述他们当天的经历，

sentences.en: which is that they were in classes in the School of International Public Affairs.
sentences.zh: 也就是他们当时正在国际公共事务学院上课。

sentences.en: And some of their peers in a classroom had stood up and pointed to other students and called them out and said,
sentences.zh: 他们班上的一些同学站了起来，指着其他同学当众质问，并说，

sentences.en: they're supporters of Hamas or they're refusing to allow, you know, our point of view to be expressed.
sentences.zh: 他们是哈马斯的同情者，或者他们拒绝让我们的观点表达出来。

sentences.en: And so, they would name names and point at each other in a classroom, which was, again, not typical protocol in classrooms at Columbia.
sentences.zh: 他们在课堂上点名并互相指责，这在哥伦比亚大学的课堂上再次打破了常规。

sentences.en: And so, they were verbally attacking or accusing one another.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们当时在言语上互相攻击或指责。

sentences.en: And they left that class to come walk, you know, two blocks to my building.
sentences.zh: 他们离开那个教室，步行穿过两个街区来到我的大楼。

sentences.en: And in front of my building, there was parked a truck.
sentences.zh: 在我大楼的前面，停着一辆卡车。

sentences.en: And it was a large truck that had four screens on the side of the back of the truck that were television screens.
sentences.zh: 那是一辆大卡车，卡车后部的侧面有四个屏幕，都是电视屏幕。

sentences.en: And this truck had been driving around the outskirts of campus and was showing either hostages that had been taken,
sentences.zh: 这辆卡车一直在校园边缘巡游，播放着被绑架者的画面，

sentences.en: Israeli hostages that had been taken by Hamas, images of these individuals,
sentences.zh: 被哈马斯绑架的以色列人质的照片，这些人的影像，

sentences.en: and images of students with their names and contact information that they say were not supporting Israel or were supporting Hamas.
sentences.zh: 以及一些学生的照片，上面带有他们的名字和联系方式，据称他们不支持以色列或支持哈马斯。

sentences.en: Other incidents like this were popping up all over the campus.
sentences.zh: 校园各处都在涌现其他类似的事件。

sentences.en: And I was teaching on the first floor.
I could, you know, see different, you know, clusters of squad cars driving past us.
sentences.zh: 我能看到一拨又一拨的警车从我们身边驶过。

sentences.en: So, the atmosphere was very tense in our room, on campus.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们教室里以及整个校园的气氛都非常紧张。

sentences.en: And they had just, you know, spent the day navigating this and came into my classroom.
sentences.zh: 他们刚刚花了一整天的时间来应对这一切，然后走进了我的课堂。

sentences.en: And they were triggered and traumatized by this.
sentences.zh: 他们因此受到了精神刺激和创伤。

sentences.en: And one of them said to me, you know, I don't know if I should stay here.
sentences.zh: 其中一个人对我说，我不知道自己是否该留在这里。

sentences.en: I didn't expect this to happen in New York.
sentences.zh: 我没想到会在纽约发生这种事。

sentences.en: And I don't know if I should even stay here.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不知道自己是否应该留在这里。

sentences.en: So, that was my experience of the first encounter with how this was playing out in campus in my class.
sentences.zh: 这就是我关于这件事如何在校园和我的课堂上发酵的第一手经历。

sentences.en: So, over the years, Peter, you have studied conflicts that you call intractable conflicts.
sentences.zh: 所以这些年来，彼得，你一直在研究你所谓的难解冲突。

sentences.en: Can you tell me what you mean by the term?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我这个词是什么意思吗？

sentences.en: There's obviously the colloquial understanding of an intractable conflict,
sentences.zh: 显然，人们对难解冲突有一个通俗的理解，

sentences.en: of, you know, a conflict that seems to drag on endlessly.
sentences.zh: 也就是看起来没完没了的冲突。

sentences.en: But you're using it, I think, in a more specific way.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你是在用一个更具体的方式来使用它。

sentences.en: Tell me what you mean by intractable conflicts.
sentences.zh: 告诉我你所说的难解冲突是什么意思。

sentences.en: Well, scholars that study these things, these, you know, long-term, difficult, demanding conflicts,
sentences.zh: 研究这些学者，也就是这些长期的、困难的、严峻的冲突的学者，

sentences.en: really see there are three qualities that distinguish them from other kinds of more manageable conflicts.
sentences.zh: 真正发现有三种特质将它们与其他更易处理的冲突区分开来。

sentences.en: One is that they tend to be highly destructive.
sentences.zh: 其中一点是它们往往具有高度的破坏性。

sentences.en: So, the intensity or the level of destructiveness can escalate and de-escalate.
sentences.zh: 因此，破坏性的强度或水平可能会升级和降级。

sentences.en: But the pattern is very destructive.
sentences.zh: 但这种模式具有很强的破坏性。

sentences.en: They tend to endure for long periods of time.
sentences.zh: 它们往往持续很长时间。

sentences.en: You know, we call them also protracted conflicts.
sentences.zh: 我们也将它们称为长期冲突。

sentences.en: They can go on for, you know, some four decades, if not more.
sentences.zh: 它们可以持续大约四十年，甚至更久。

sentences.en: And most importantly, in terms of diagnosing them or understanding them as intractable,
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，就诊断它们或将其理解为难解冲突而言，

sentences.en: is they have a history, often, where there have been many good faith attempts to address them
sentences.zh: 是它们通常有着一段历史，期间有过许多出于善意的尝试来解决它们

sentences.en: They may be informal or negotiation processes.
sentences.zh: 它们可能是非正式的或谈判过程。

sentences.en: But they have a history of attempts to end them that either seem to have no effect or actually backfire.
sentences.zh: 但它们有试图结束这些冲突的历史，这些尝试要么看起来毫无效果，要么实际上适得其反。

sentences.en: And so, yes, they have that kind of quality where they bring things in.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，它们具有那种将各种事情卷入其中的特质。

sentences.en: And I have to say, it's, you know, they sometimes feel like a storm,
sentences.zh: 我必须说，有时它们感觉就像一场风暴，

sentences.en: like a hurricane that gathers and has that kind of force that's bigger than us.
sentences.zh: 就像一场汇聚并具有超越我们力量的飓风。

sentences.en: To step away from what's happening in the Middle East for a second,
sentences.zh: 暂时撇开中东正在发生的事情不谈，

sentences.en: to look at another conflict that I think many Americans are seeing,
sentences.zh: 来看另一个许多美国人都看到的冲突，

sentences.en: many people feel like the partisan divide in our country is getting deeper
sentences.zh: 许多人觉得我们国家的党派分歧正在加深，

sentences.en: and it feels like an intractable conflict.
sentences.zh: 而且这感觉像是一场难解的冲突。

sentences.en: Now, thankfully, for the most part, I don't think it devolves into violence,
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地，在大多数情况下，我认为它并没有演变成暴力，

sentences.en: at least at the level of violence that you see in geopolitical conflicts and war.
sentences.zh: 至少没有达到你在地缘政治冲突和战争中看到的暴力程度。

sentences.en: But there have been times in the United States, in the history of the United States,
sentences.zh: 但在美国历史上，曾有那么一些时刻，

sentences.en: where conflict between Americans has resulted in war.
sentences.zh: 美国人之间的冲突导致了战争。

sentences.en: Can you talk about whether partisanship qualifies as the kind of intractable conflict
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈党派之争是否符合你所说的这种难解冲突吗？
事实上，情况变得更糟糕了吗？

sentences.en: And in fact, has it gotten worse?
sentences.zh: 这难道不是难解冲突的一个例子吗？

sentences.en: Is it an example of intractable conflict?
sentences.zh: 我确实认为这是一个例子。

sentences.en: I do think it is an example.
sentences.zh: 这也是我现在看待美国政治极化的方式。

sentences.en: And it is how I think about political polarization in the U.S.

用某些标准来衡量，这大约是一个持续了60年的轨迹，

sentences.zh: 红州与蓝州美国人之间的敌意和疏离感不断加剧，

sentences.en: of increasing enmity and distance between red and blue Americans,

这肯定发生在过去的20年里。
